terrain/earth/snow is counted under planet_earth after Mars entry because Mars loads that sheet itself. It is not the SceneDirector preload, and Residency is not attributing a session handle to planet_earth.

Mars's material list includes TileId.Snow (C:\dev\universegame\Assets\_Game\Code\Runtime\Terrain\TerrainStreamer.cs:161, comment at :160: Mars's CO2 frost uses Snow). TileId 5 maps to ArtKeys.Terrain.EarthSnow = "terrain/earth/snow" (C:\dev\universegame\Assets\_Game\Code\Runtime\Terrain\TerrainTiles.cs:9 and :23; C:\dev\universegame\Assets\_Game\Code\Runtime\Art\ArtKeys.cs:40). There is no terrain/mars/snow or frost sheet. When Mars's TerrainStreamer.Begin runs (TerrainStreamer.cs:71-72), TerrainTileSet.Load (C:\dev\universegame\Assets\_Game\Code\Runtime\Terrain\TerrainTileSet.cs:49) calls ArtLoad.Asset("terrain/earth/snow"). That goes to Residency.Track(key) and GroupOf: the "terrain" case returns "planet_" plus the second segment, which is "planet_earth" (C:\dev\universegame\Assets\_Game\Code\Runtime\Perf\Residency.cs:20 and :118-119). The asset really is in the planet_earth Addressables group (C:\dev\universegame\Assets\AddressableAssetsData\AssetGroups\planet_earth.asset:28-29, BundleMode 0 = PackTogether). So the one remaining planet_earth holder is Mars's own live TileSet, and it is released when Mars unloads (TerrainStreamer.cs:417 and :420, TerrainTileSet.cs:159). It is a planet attribution problem, not a leak.

Why it is not the preload: ArtLoad.Session tracks the handle with group "session" (C:\dev\universegame\Assets\_Game\Code\Runtime\Art\ArtLoad.cs:55). Because the key argument is null, the key is also stored as "session" (Residency.cs:25). PlanetOf("session") returns null (Residency.cs:88). So a session entry can never appear in CountPlanet("planet_earth") or in Holders("planet_earth") as "terrain/earth/snow".

The probe logs prove it. In C:\dev\universegame\logs\memory_probe_20261106_164339.jsonl and C:\dev\universegame\logs\memory_probe_20261106_163535.jsonl, the Space leg shows prevGroup planet_earth, prevHandles 0, holders "none", and planet_earth is not among the resident groups. On the Mars leg planet_earth is resident again, with 1 handle: terrain/earth/snow. The session preload did not change between those two legs, so the count came back with Mars's own load.

The earlier count of 7 fits the same explanation. Before commit 96112df, Prune dropped an entry only when its handle was no longer valid (Residency.cs:129-133). The session preload keeps the shared Addressables operation alive, so Earth's six released TileSet handles stayed valid. That gives 6 Earth entries plus Mars's snow entry, 7 in all. The 11:13 PlayMode run shows the same pattern: snow x20 against x18 for the other Earth sheets (C:\dev\universegame\coordination\reports\unity\tests_2026-11-06.md:54). Once 96112df routed every release through ArtLoad.Release and Untrack (ArtLoad.cs:42-47, Residency.cs:29-33), only Mars's live handle is left.

The current status note is wrong. C:\dev\universegame\coordination\status\UNITY_STATUS.md:4 blames the session preload "under the planet group". Keying the preload by planet and releasing it on transition would not change this count. ResidencyTests will keep failing at C:\dev\universegame\Assets\_Game\Tests\Unit\Play\ResidencyTests.cs:121-122 until Mars stops loading an Earth-addressed sheet, or until the group/attribution rule changes. Options: give Mars its own frost key, move the snow sheet to a shared group in both ArtRules.GroupFor and Residency.GroupOf, or treat a planet's own TileSet loads as that planet's.

Accounting model:
- ArtLoad.Asset(key) tracks under GroupOf(key) (ArtLoad.cs:14-19).
- ArtLoad.Asset(location, key) tracks under GroupOf of the key passed in (ArtLoad.cs:22-27).
- ArtLoad.Assets(label, group) tracks under the explicit group, with the label as key (ArtLoad.cs:30-35).
- ArtLoad.Session(key) tracks under "session" with key "session" (ArtLoad.cs:52-57).
- ArtLoad.Release returns early if the handle is invalid, otherwise Untracks it and calls Addressables.Release (ArtLoad.cs:42-47).
- Untrack removes the last entry whose handle is Equal (Residency.cs:29-33). Equal means same operation and version, and Addressables gives every holder of the same key and type the same cached operation and version.
- Count, CountPlanet, Holders, ResidentGroups and OnlyPlanet all call Prune first.
- PlanetOf maps "planet_<id>" and "planet_<id>_*" to a planet for every PlanetId. Anything else (session, common, ui, icons, space, planet_space, planet_waystation, planet_warden, planet_rig) maps to null (Residency.cs:86-95).
- GroupOf (Residency.cs:109-127) is meant to mirror ArtRules.GroupFor but has no "flora" case (C:\dev\universegame\Assets\_Game\Code\Editor\ArtRules.cs:110), so flora/<planet>/* is counted as "common".

- TerrainTileSet.kept (18 session terrain sheets for Earth, Mars, Mercury and Venus)
- FilmFeature's three session overlay textures
- FxSheet.cache

- MenuController title art
- SpaceWorld, SpaceBackdrop, DockingBay and Waystation (Space scene)

Everything else (CreatureDirector, PoiPlacer, StageLayers, DepthBands, PlanetBackdrop, ParallaxLayers, FloraRigs, GroundStrip, SpriteCharacterView, ModelView and ModelSwap instances, PlayerView, ShipLegsView, RigToolView, DustStorm, BaseBuilder, CataloguePanel) is a PlanetSide instance that releases in OnDestroy or Clear. The DontDestroyOnLoad objects (MemoryProbe, PostFx) hold no art. No file was edited.

risks: The planet_earth acceptance check after Mars entry (ResidencyTests.cs:122) cannot pass while Mars's material list contains TileId.Snow (TerrainStreamer.cs:161) and that id maps to an Earth-addressed asset (TerrainTiles.cs:23, planet_earth.asset:28-29). Removing or re-keying the SceneDirector preload (SceneDirector.cs:31-34) does not change this count. The status note at UNITY_STATUS.md:4 points U-091 at the wrong fix.

If the session preload is removed, Mars's terrain/earth/snow load opens the whole planet_earth bundle on its own (BundleMode 0 = PackTogether). Today that bundle is already open all session because of the preload, so the snow handle costs no extra memory.

Untrack has an ordering hazard. Handles to the same key and type are Equal across holders: Addressables reuses one cached operation (AddressablesImpl.cs:579-608; ResourceManager.cs:350-352; equality in AsyncOperationHandle.cs:415-418). Untrack removes the last Equal entry (Residency.cs:31-32). If a session entry were ever added after a planet entry for the same operation (a lazy Preload, or Session called mid-run), the planet holder's release would remove the session entry and leave a phantom planet entry that Prune never clears, because the session keeps the operation valid. Safe today only because Preload runs in SceneDirector.Start before the first LoadPlanetSide (lines 31-34 then 49), and keptIds deduplicates.

Residency.GroupOf has no 'flora' case, while ArtRules.GroupFor maps flora to planet_<x> (ArtRules.cs:110). FloraRigs handles for flora/earth/rigset (FloraRigs.cs:92, CartoonStage.cs:70) are counted as common, so a leaked rig set would never fail CountPlanet or OnlyPlanet (a false negative).

ItemIcons (ItemIcons.cs:36) never releases its handles. The aerostat_deck icon key props/venus/aerostat_deck (ItemRegistry.cs:77) is grouped planet_venus. Opening the inventory, crafting or catalogue panel with that item on another planet pins a planet_venus handle for the whole session and makes OnlyPlanet false everywhere.

In StageLayers.Request, the manifest probe callback (StageLayers.cs:167-172) lacks the live-set guard that the label probe has (line 162). A set released while its manifest probe is in flight leaks a manifestHandle under planet_<planet> that no Clear or ReleaseSet can reach.
SpriteCharacterView.Load (lines 60-82) and GroundStrip.Load (line 43) can orphan a handle if Load runs twice before the first load completes. Today each runs once per scene load, so this is latent.

Persistent non-Addressables textures add a fixed amount to every scene's texture and working-set numbers, and Residency does not see them. None of them use mip streaming (streamingMipmaps 0), so the 512 MB streaming budget does not cover them: session terrain sheets about 48 MB (18 x 1024 px BC7 + BC5 with mips), ArtMaterials block textures about 43 MB (126 x 512 px), and TerrainBlockPalette real arrays about 44 MB, which survive the Space hop until the next planet. All sizes are estimated from texture dimensions and formats, not measured.
ResidencyTests measures BudgetMonitor systemMemoryMB (ResidencyTests.cs:99, :130), not the workingSetMB that D-089's 'working set within 10 %' names (BudgetMonitor.cs:21, :125).

Residency.entries, TerrainTileSet.kept/keptIds, FxSheet.cache, ItemIcons and FilmFeature are statics that persist across PlayMode tests in one run (one domain per run). The 11:13 report's x18/x20 counts come from that accumulation before Untrack existed (tests_2026-11-06.md:54). Any test that leaves a holder alive will pollute ResidencyTests.

risks: The computed task's 'mip budget was 384 MB' is stale. The repo has streamingMipmapsMemoryBudget 1536 at all 6 levels (QualitySettings.asset:42,95,148,201,254,307), and TASK_BOARD.md:293 itself says the Goal's '1.5 GB mip budget'. The change is 1536 -> 512 on six lines. No test asserts these values today.

With a 512 MB mip budget, non-streaming textures still count against the budget. Only model maps stream: 332 metas with streamingMipmaps: 1, about 635 MB stored across all groups. Everything else (2D sheets, v3, backgrounds, block arrays, render textures) is non-streaming. streamingMipmapsMaxLevelReduction is 2 (QualitySettings.asset:44 etc.), so streaming maps can drop by at most 2 mips. The per-planet import cap of 512 MB plus common (~173 MB formula), planet_space and space (~83 MB) and the session terrain sheets can therefore exceed the D-089 'textures <= 512 MB loaded' row, even though no single planet exceeds 512 MB.

Rejection in OnPreprocessTexture is log-only. ArtImporter.cs:185-188 returns without changing settings, and PassesValidation (ArtImporter.cs:758-769) does not re-check the cap. The rejected texture is still registered and addressed (ArtImporter.cs:665) with leftover or default settings. A per-planet 512 MB cap must also be checked in PassesValidation, or the rejected key must be unaddressed.

The current cap check is skipped for v3 assets (the ConfigureV3 early return at ArtImporter.cs:179) and for block textures (the early return at ArtImporter.cs:159-163). StageLayerBytes scans only Art/backgrounds and Art/props (ArtImporter.cs:389). Block paths (terrain/

//top_color.png) also fail TryParse at line 396. A per-planet sum must add terrain, creatures and flora and handle IsBlockTexture (ArtRules.cs:46-57) separately.

StoredBytes (ArtRules.cs:180) always applies 4/3 for mips, but v3 assets have no mips (ArtImporter.cs:279) and NPOT art has no mips (ArtImporter.cs:195). The formula therefore over-counts those by up to 33 %. Per planet the gap between the formula and a meta-aware estimate is only 0-4 % today (Venus 221.8 vs 218.0 MB). Sprite-atlas members are packed into atlas pages at build time, so the real cost can differ from the sum of source sizes.

StageLayerBytes re-walks every PNG under backgrounds and props for each stage-layer import, so Reimport All is O(N²). A per-planet version that also scans terrain, creatures and flora (~926 Art PNGs) on each import would be slower. Caching per planet, or scanning only that planet's folders, would avoid that.

Residency.GroupOf (runtime, Residency.cs:109-127) has no 'flora' case, while ArtRules.GroupFor (Editor, ArtRules.cs:110) maps flora/

to planet_

. Runtime handles on flora/earth/* are therefore counted as 'common' and never appear in CountPlanet/Holders for the planet.

Cross-planet terrain keys mean releasing on transition cannot clear the planet_earth count while on Mars: terrain/earth/snow is loaded by Mars (TerrainStreamer.cs:161). The same holds for planet_jupiter while on Saturn, Uranus or Neptune (floe keys, TerrainStreamer.cs:159). The ResidencyTests criterion '0 handles within 5 s' needs one of: a Mars-owned or shared key for frost, or attributing handles by the loading planet rather than the key's group.

Block textures for all four solid planets (~42 MB) stay resident through the Resources registry (ArtMaterials.cs:57). Earth's block arrays survive the Earth -> Space hop (TerrainBlockPalette.cs:71-75). Both push against 'working set returns within 10 % of first visit' and the textures row, and Residency handle counts see neither.

Changing the cap constant or message needs no ArtImporter.GetVersion bump (currently 13 at ArtImporter.cs:24). The rule decides rejection only, not import output. A bump would force a reimport of all ~926 Art PNGs.

plan.rootCause:
The planet_earth handle still held 5 s after Mars entry is not a release failure, and the SceneDirector preload is not the holder. Mars's own tile set loads it. TerrainStreamer.MaterialsFor(Mars) includes TileId.Snow (C:\dev\universegame\Assets\_Game\Code\Runtime\Terrain\TerrainStreamer.cs:161). Id 5 maps to the Earth key "terrain/earth/snow" (TerrainTiles.cs:23, ArtKeys.cs:40). TerrainTileSet.Load tracks that key with ArtLoad.Asset (TerrainTileSet.cs:49), and Residency.GroupOf files every terrain/earth/* key under planet_earth (Residency.cs:118-119). The asset really is an entry of the planet_earth Addressables group (AssetGroups/planet_earth.asset:29), which is Pack Together. So while the player is on Mars, the whole Earth bundle stays open and ResidencyTests.cs:122 can never reach 0. The giants have the same problem: Saturn, Uranus and Neptune load terrain/jupiter/floe_*.

The session preload (SceneDirector.cs:31-34, TerrainTileSet.Preload) is tracked as "session", so it never shows up in CountPlanet. It is still a separate D-089 problem: it keeps the Earth, Mars, Mercury and Venus bundles and 18 non-streamed sheets (about 48 MB) open for the whole session, hidden from the handle check. The fix has three parts:
1. Move the shared sheets into "common", in the data and in a single group table used by the importer and by Residency.
2. Replace the session preload with a per-planet prefetch that starts when an entry starts, while the iris closes (0.35 s, off the load's critical path). The planet's TileSet then takes over those handles. The previous planet's sheets are already released on leave by TerrainStreamer.OnDestroy → TileSet.Dispose.
3. Bring the budgets, probe, gate, importer cap and mip budget up to D-089.

Corrections to the computed task: the mip budget in the repo is 1536 MB at all six quality levels, not 384 MB (U-086 set 1536). The status line at coordination/status/UNITY_STATUS.md:4 blames the wrong holder.

problems.problem: The widened cap is not order-stable. Once a planet's textures pass 512 MB, every texture of that planet fails OverPlanetCap on its next import, not just the newest one. Because PassesValidation now also refuses, a Reimport All or a Library rebuild would leave the whole planet with Unity's default import, not as sprites, and its sheet loads would fail.
problems.evidence: The planned PlanetTextureBytes(planet, except) follows StageLayerBytes (ArtImporter.cs:386-399): it adds every PNG of the planet on disk except the file being imported, so others + self equals the total for every file. OnPreprocessTexture returns before any configuration on rejection (pattern at ArtImporter.cs:181-190). The old cap had the same flaw but covered only stage layers; the new one covers sheets, models and block textures.
problems.fix: Only reject a texture that has no Addressables entry or importer settings yet. Or sum the planet in a stable order (already-addressed files first, then by path) and reject only the files past the cap.

problems.problem: The per-import cap scan opens every PNG of the planet each time a texture imports, and does it again in postprocess. The plan leaves the size cache optional and estimates the cost as 'seconds'.
problems.evidence: There are 923 Art PNGs, 112-134 per inner planet (counted under terrain, creatures, flora, props and backgrounds for each planet). PngSize opens each file (ArtImporter.cs:403-418) in OnPreprocessTexture (:152, once per texture) and again through PassesValidation in OnPostprocessAllAssets (:639). A Reimport All therefore costs about 150k-200k file opens on the 8 GB Windows laptop, which runs under a 20-minute job cap (U-023).
problems.fix: Make the cache required: a per-planet total keyed by path and LastWriteTimeUtc, built once per import batch and cleared in OnPostprocessAllAssets. Do not scan the directories for every texture.
